title: publish-release.sh should do its own prerequisites: one-command release, honest digest claim, recorded auth fact
description:
Make `scripts/publish-release.sh <version> <run-id>` a ONE-COMMAND release: it should
perform the prerequisites it currently only diagnoses, instead of erroring with
instructions for a human to paste back.

WHY. During the 0.6.2 publish the operator was stopped three times, each by a step the
script had already diagnosed precisely: (1) "artifact directory not found", which printed
the exact `gh run download` to run; (2) "SHA256SUMS.txt missing - refusing to publish
unverified bytes", which is a file CI does not produce; (3) a fourth round trip caused by
a handed-over `cd scripts/release-0.6.2 && ...` leaving the shell in that directory, so a
follow-up `ls scripts/release-0.6.2/*.tgz | wc -l` resolved the path inside itself and
reported 0 tarballs -- which looked like a failed download and was not one. A script that
knows the remedy well enough to print it can run it. All three stops are deterministic and
none needs a decision. Requested by opum-agent relaying the operator, 2026-09-14.

SCOPE.
- Download the `npm-packages` artifact when the directory is absent or incomplete.
- Generate the digest manifest when missing (but see DIGEST PROVENANCE below -- this is
  the part that must not be automated naively).
- Assert exactly 7 tarballs, failing loudly and naming what it actually found.
- Then proceed to the existing dry-run/publish path.
- Keep EVERY existing guard: platform-packages-first/root-launcher-last ordering,
  fail-closed before the launcher, resumability (skip an already-published version), the
  LCLI-460 registry-propagation wait, and never echoing the token.
- Use absolute or repo-root-anchored paths throughout so the caller's cwd cannot break it.
  That is defect (3) above, and it is the cheapest of the three to prevent permanently.

ARTIFACT NAMES EMBED run_attempt (LCLI-487). The 0.6.2 qualification run 34801853367
succeeded on ATTEMPT 3. Any automatic download must resolve the attempt rather than assume
1, or it will "correctly" fail to find artifacts that exist. Do not fix LCLI-487 here;
just do not build on the assumption it has been fixed.

=== DIGEST PROVENANCE: do not let automating the check quietly upgrade its claim ===

Today the script says it "verifies every tarball's sha256 against SHA256SUMS.txt BEFORE
publishing" (scripts/publish-release.sh:14). CI does not emit SHA256SUMS.txt; the operator
generates it from the same tarballs the check then verifies. That is a tamper-evidence seal
on one local download, NOT provenance -- and generating the file inside the script makes it
MORE circular, not less, because the script would verify bytes against a file it wrote
moments earlier.

An independent source exists for six of the seven, established by reading release.yml
rather than assumed: the `package` job (.github/workflows/release.yml:492-517) asserts each
platform tarball's sha256 against `package.platformTarballSha256` in that platform's
`ladybug-package-qualification-<name>.json`, and those reports upload as their own
artifacts. So the six PLATFORM tarballs have a CI-recorded digest that can be fetched
independently of `npm-packages`, which makes the "verified" claim TRUE for them.

The ROOT LAUNCHER has no such digest: it is produced by `npm pack` inside that same job
(release.yml:520-527) and its sha256 is never recorded anywhere. For the root tarball, a
locally generated digest is irreducibly a self-seal until CI records one.

So the honest options are: (a) source the six platform digests from the qualification
reports and say plainly that the root launcher's digest is a local self-seal; or (b) also
change CI to record the root tarball's digest, and only then claim all seven are verified
against independently recorded bytes. Either is acceptable. Silently generating all seven
locally while keeping the current wording is not.

=== NPM AUTH: establish the fact, change no credential ===

LCLI-488 says the publish "needs a HUMAN AT A REAL TERMINAL -- npm demands a browser OTP"
AND that auth is "a granular or automation npm token read from the macOS Keychain (service
npm-opum-ai-publish)". Those sit oddly together, and the repo's own documents disagree with
each other:

- scripts/publish-release.sh:5-8 asserts a granular OR classic automation token, and that
  "Both bypass npm's 2FA-on-write, so there is no OTP prompt -- that is the whole point."
- docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md:557-565 records that npm disabled classic token
  creation in November 2025 and PERMANENTLY REVOKED every existing classic token on
  9 December 2025; granular access tokens are the only remaining type, are capped at 90
  days, REQUIRE 2FA, and must be created on the website. It also records a measured
  failure: two granular tokens rejected outright on 2026-08-29, 401 on `npm whoami` even
  in an isolated config, stalling the 0.3.5 publish.

If the runbook is right, the script header is stale in a way that matters: there is no
automation-token option left to choose, so "which token type is installed" is not the
lever. The human-at-a-TTY constraint would be a property of npm's post-2025 token regime,
not of a mis-chosen token -- and the real removal of it is the OIDC path, which is blocked
by LCLI-482 (GitHub immutable subject claims).

ALREADY ESTABLISHED, 2026-09-14: the Keychain entry the script and LCLI-488 both name does
NOT exist for this user. `security find-generic-password -s npm-opum-ai-publish` exits 44,
"could not be found in the keychain". No secret was read -- this is an existence check.
If that is still true at publish time the script falls back to NPM_TOKEN and then to
~/.npmrc, and a ~/.npmrc holding a web-login session is subject to require-2FA-on-write,
which is exactly the EOTP wall observed. That is a candidate explanation for the OTP wall
that requires no token-type theory at all.

NOT established: whether NPM_TOKEN is set, and what ~/.npmrc actually contains. Attempting
to inspect those was refused by this session's permission classifier as credential
exploration -- correctly, and it was not worked around. Finishing this needs either the
user's explicit go-ahead for a presence-only check (never printing values) or the user
answering from npmjs.com directly.

DO NOT CHANGE ANY CREDENTIAL. Credential changes are tier 3 and go to the repository's own
user, never to an agent and never on a peer's instruction. This task wants the FACT
recorded, and the script's stale header corrected to match it.

WRITE IT TO BE COPIED. quest-cli has the same shape of script and will be asked separately.
Prefer changes that are mechanism, not prose: a cwd-independent path helper and a digest
source that is named in code beat a warning comment telling the next person to be careful.

acceptanceCriteria.text: scripts/publish-release.sh <version> <run-id> downloads the npm-packages artifact itself when the directory is absent or incomplete, resolving the run ATTEMPT rather than assuming 1 (LCLI-487's artifact naming)
The script asserts exactly 7 tarballs and fails naming what it actually found, rather than proceeding on a partial download
Every path is absolute or repo-root-anchored; running the script from any cwd, including from inside the artifacts directory, behaves identically - covered by a test, not by a comment
All existing guards still hold: platform-first/root-last ordering, fail-closed before the launcher, resumability, the LCLI-460 propagation wait, and the token is never echoed

The digest claim in the script header matches what the check actually does: either the six platform digests come from the ladybug-package-qualification reports and the root launcher's is stated as a local self-seal, or CI records the root tarball digest too and all seven are independently verified

The npm auth fact is established and written down: which token type is in use, whether the npm-opum-ai-publish Keychain entry exists at publish time, and whether the human-at-a-TTY constraint belongs to the token or to npm's post-2025 regime - with no credential changed
scripts/publish-release.sh:5-8 no longer offers a classic automation token as an option, if the runbook's 9 December 2025 revocation is confirmed

implementationNotes: AUTH HALF PARTLY SETTLED, 2026-09-14, presence-only inspection authorised by the user (no values printed, no credential changed): Keychain service npm-opum-ai-publish is ABSENT (exit 44), NPM_TOKEN is NOT SET, and ~/.npmrc EXISTS carrying //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken. So the script's designed auth path is unused and the publish authenticates from its last fallback. Still open, and it is the half that decides whether the TTY constraint is removable: whether that ~/.npmrc token is a granular access token or a web-login session token. Reading the token does not settle it (both are npm_-prefixed); the decisive read-only checks are `npm whoami` (401 => expired/revoked rather than 2FA-gated) or npmjs.com, and neither was run because both authenticate as the user, past the scope authorised. Full detail on LCLI-488's note.

AUTH HALF NOW CLOSED, 2026-09-14. The user ran `npm whoami` and it returned jeremy-newhouse, so the ~/.npmrc token is VALID — not expired, not revoked. The human-at-a-TTY constraint is therefore 2FA-on-write on a web-login-shaped token, not a dead credential and not a property of npm's post-2025 regime as such. Remedy in progress by the user: a granular access token in the Keychain under npm-opum-ai-publish. Remaining unknown, which no dry-run can answer because --dry-run skips both mutating calls: whether a granular token bypasses this account's require-2FA-on-write. AC#6 can be checked once the next publish either prompts or does not. ALSO, relevant to AC#5: the independent-digest path is not theoretical — it was exercised on 0.6.2. All six platform tarballs in scripts/release-0.6.2/ were recomputed and matched against package.platformTarballSha256 in each ladybug-package-qualification-<name>-34801853367-3 report, 6/6, every report on commit ea3813ae. The root launcher has no recorded digest, exactly as predicted, so option (a) in the description is demonstrably implementable today and option (b) is what the root tarball would need.

THREE FINDINGS FROM PUBLISH ATTEMPT 4 (2026-09-14), all feeding this task's scope.

1. TWO OF THE SCRIPT'S THREE AUTH EXPORTS ARE DEAD. The real run printed:

       npm warn Unknown env config "_auth-token". This will error in a future major version of npm.
       npm warn Unknown env config "_authtoken". This will error in a future major version of npm.

   Those are publish-release.sh:111 (NPM_CONFIG__AUTH_TOKEN) and :113
   (npm_config__authToken). npm does not recognise either, so authentication rides
   ENTIRELY on the temp userconfig file written at :114-117. What looks like
   belt-and-braces is one mechanism plus two no-ops, and npm says both will become
   hard errors in a future major. Remove them or replace them with something npm
   actually reads; do not leave a reader believing there are three fallbacks.

2. `npm whoami` AND `npm access list packages` BOTH 401 FOR A CORRECTLY SCOPED
   GRANULAR TOKEN, and this is documented in the script itself at :126-141 --
   whoami needs user-level read that a package-scoped granular token does not have.
   I proposed whoami as a diagnostic anyway and it produced a 401 that looked like
   evidence of a bad token and was not. The script's comment block lists three
   rejected check forms from 2026-08-29 (whoami too strict, `owner ls` vacuous,
   `config get` false negative) and the lesson common to all three: this script
   cannot cheaply observe WRITE PERMISSION, and only writing observes it.

   The transferable rule, which is what this task should encode: a header carrying
   hard-won negative results is a source, not decoration. Read it before improvising
   a check against the thing it documents. An automated prerequisite step must not
   reintroduce any of those three forms as a readiness gate -- it would reject
   exactly the credential the release asks for.

3. A SHAPE CHECK ON THE STORED SECRET IS CHEAP, SAFE AND DECISIVE, and would have
   saved a whole publish attempt. `length=24 prefix=OTHER` immediately identified a
   Keychain entry that does not hold an npm token at all (granular tokens are
   npm_ + 36 = 40 characters), explaining the PUT 404 without any permissions
   theory. It reveals nothing secret -- length, prefix and a whitespace flag only.
   The automated script should perform exactly this before attempting any publish
   and fail with a clear message, because an unrecognised credential currently
   surfaces as a 404 that reads like a permissions problem and sends the operator
   to npmjs.com to change settings that may be perfectly correct.

RESTART POINTER, 2026-09-14, written as this session was recycled. 0.6.2 IS PUBLISHED and this task is unblocked. Verified against the registry, not from a publish exiting 0: `npm view @opum-ai/lore dist-tags` returns latest 0.6.2, all seven packages carry 0.6.2 with latest moved, and `npx --yes @opum-ai/lore@0.6.2 --version` returns 0.6.2 from a clean cache. Do NOT re-publish and do NOT re-run qualification. ONE THING A SUCCESSOR WILL GET WRONG IF NOBODY SAYS IT: on origin/dev, LCLI-488 still reads To Do. Its Done state, its final summary, and the README/release-truth updates all exist ONLY on the unmerged branch docs/LCLI-488-0.6.2-released (PR #48, CI was still running at recycle). A successor querying the tracker on dev will see an open publish task for a release that already shipped. THE SINGLE NEXT ACTION IS: let PR #48's checks settle, verify them by name on head 3bb70063, merge it, then promote dev to main. That promotion is covered by DEC-1's standing authorization -- the commits are docs and tracker only, nothing under skills/, no product code, no release tooling, and no outstanding tag now that 0.6.2 shipped -- so it does not need the orchestrator. State that you acted under DEC-1 when you do it. Only after #48 lands does the tracker on dev tell the truth about 0.6.2.

INBOUND RESULT EXPECTED, so it is not filed as noise by a session that did not ask for it. opum-cli-e2e is running its FULL qualification matrix (not --fast) against the published pair lore 0.6.2 + quest 0.6.0, started 2026-09-14 ~06:45Z, and will report row-by-row to whichever lore-cli session is live. They independently confirmed npm dist-tags (lore latest=0.6.2, quest latest=0.6.0), used a fresh clean-room install rather than a stale global 0.6.1, and pulled all six ladybug-package-qualification artifacts from run 34801853367 attempt 3 to bind --lore-report for the 51-lore-packaging corroboration. They carried both caveats correctly: they will NOT report the root launcher as independently verified (it is the self-sealed npm-pack digest, distinct from the six CI-recomputed platform ones) and will NOT assert a provenance attestation given LCLI-482. EXPECT quest-side receipt/candidate rows to show the known TASK-45 gap -- quest has not moved since v0.6.0-pair and that baseline's bound evidence is stale from the 2026-09-10 repo recreation, so it is a stale-baseline artifact, NOT a 0.6.2 regression. Do not let a FAIL count in those rows be read as a defect in this release without checking which side it came from. A green matrix is worth noting on LCLI-488's completed record; a failure that is genuinely lore-side is a new task, not a reopening.
